title: After going somewhere, the files of the place just left stay listed and usable under the new place's name until it answers: up to a minute for Recents
problem: Found by the reviewer of 'show-in-enclosing-folder-key' (done record: /home/user/polish-tools/done/show-in-enclosing-folder-key.json, first item under 'Found, not fixed', and its review_fixes), and read in the code by the orchestrator. `location_changed` (src/finder/mod.rs) clears the selection and calls `load_listing(select, false, cx)`, which sets `self.loading = true` and replaces `self.listing` and the rows only when the background read answers. Until then the rows on screen are those of the place the window left, drawn under the new place's title, sidebar selection and path bar, and treated by every command under the new place's rules (`in_trash()`, `shows_parent_column()`, `current_folder()`). For a folder on a local disk that is a few milliseconds. For Recents it lasts until the index is ready (`engine.wait_ready(Duration::from_secs(60))` in `load_listing`), which is up to a minute after launch or after a search location is added; for a folder on a slow network volume it lasts as long as the read. What the reviewer probed: Trash, then Recents, before the listing arrived: the Trash's item was still listed and could be selected, its right-click menu was the ordinary item menu (Open With, Rename…, Move to Trash) instead of the Trash's, and before the guard added in that review Show in Enclosing Folder opened the Trash's own storage folder as an ordinary folder. By reading only, not probed: the other way round, a folder's rows under the Trash get the Trash's menu, with Delete Immediately… one confirmation away. 'show-in-enclosing-folder-key' guards its one command (`enclosing_target()` returns nothing while `self.loading && !self.is_searching()`); nothing else is guarded. Besides what can be done to the wrong files, the window is plainly misleading in that time: it says Recents and lists the last folder's files.
proposal: Reproduce first, headlessly: Trash (or a folder), then Recents with an index that is not ready (tests/finder.rs cmd_return_leaves_an_item_of_the_trash_alone_while_the_next_place_is_read shows how to hold a listing back: its second assertion is exactly this premise), and show that the old place's row is listed, can be selected with a click and with Down, gets a context menu, and can be opened. Then decide what the file area does between leaving a place and the new place's answer, and make every view (icons, list, columns, gallery) follow it. Two things must hold. (1) The old place's rows can never be acted on once the window has left: not selected by pointer or keys (arrows, Cmd+A, type to select), not opened, not given a menu, not dragged, not a drop target, not renamed. Find the choke points rather than guarding commands one by one; with no selection possible most commands are inert by themselves, so the pointer handlers of rows and the selection keys are what matters. (2) No new flicker: today a folder on a local disk goes straight from the old rows to the new ones, and a file area that is blank for a frame or two on every step would be worse than the bug for everyday use. So measure it: count the frames between the navigation and the new rows for a local folder, and look at what a user would see. One shape that satisfies both: the rows are dropped from the model at once (so nothing can touch them) while the views keep painting the last frame's rows, inert, for a short grace period (on the order of 150 ms), after which the area shows that the place is being read (blank with the views' usual frame, or the placeholders a search uses; read 'search-skeleton-flash' and, if on the trunk, 'empty-state-messages' and 'search-start-no-flash' for how those are drawn and timed). Another: clear the rows at once, if you can show that the new rows of a local folder arrive before the next frame is painted. A place whose read fails still shows its error as now. The empty-state message ('This folder is empty' and its relatives) must not flash while a place is being read: `self.rows.is_empty() && !self.loading` guards it today; keep that true. When the rows of the left place can no longer be acted on, the guard in `enclosing_target()` is redundant: remove it or keep it, and say which; the test cmd_return_leaves_an_item_of_the_trash_alone_while_the_next_place_is_read asserts that the Trash's item is still listed right after Cmd+Shift+F, which fails by design if the rows go away at once: rewrite it to assert the new behaviour (the item cannot be selected) or delete it, and say so.
original_test_plan: Headless UI tests that fail today, with a listing held back (Recents with an index that isn't ready is the long case; find or build a way to hold a folder's read back too, or say why you couldn't): after leaving the Trash for Recents, and after leaving a folder for the Trash, a click on where the old row was selects nothing, Down and Cmd+A select nothing, a right-click opens no item menu of the old row, Return and a double-click open nothing; when the listing answers, the new place's rows are there and work, and a `select` passed to the navigation (Back to a folder selects where you came from) still selects. A frames test for flicker: a step between two local folders never paints a frame with an empty file area and no placeholder, or whatever your design promises. The four views each. A search started while a place is still being read shows the search's results, not the old rows (`drop_stale_results` already empties the rows when a search starts; keep it working). Pictures: the file area in the waiting state, light and dark, in the list and icon views.
original_risks: Every navigation goes through this path, so a mistake here is felt everywhere: flicker on each folder step, a selection that Back used to restore and no longer does, a scroll position lost, the column view's panes (cleared in `location_changed`, rebuilt from the rows) drawn empty for a moment, quiet reloads (Refresh, file operations, the index finishing) wrongly treated as leaving a place (`loading` is set only when `quiet` is false; keep quiet reloads untouched). `loading` is also read by `check_for_changes` paths (two places near load_folder_stats) and the empty-state condition. Tabs and split view each have their own Finder; a pane must not blank because the other one navigated.

verifier.claim_check: Not checked by a second reviewer. The reviewer of 'show-in-enclosing-folder-key' probed the Trash-to-Recents case and committed a test whose premise it is; the orchestrator read `location_changed` and `load_listing` on the trunk (the rows are replaced only in the listing task's answer; Recents waits up to 60 s for the index). The folder-under-the-Trash case is by reading only. Reproduce before changing anything; if you cannot, write the closed record and return skipped with the evidence.
verifier.implementation_notes: See the proposal: a starting point, not a checked plan. If the only certainly-right change within reach is smaller (for instance making the old rows inert while a place is read, without changing what is painted), do that and say what you left; a smaller change that is certainly right beats a larger one that is probably right.

orchestrator_notes: 'empty-state-messages' works in the same condition (what the file area says when it lists nothing) and comes before this one in lane c; read its done record. 'search-start-no-flash' comes after and will build on what you decide. The reviewer who found this wrote, for whoever takes it: 'If you clear the rows on leaving a place (which would fix it for every command), that assertion fails by design: delete the test then. The `loading` check in `enclosing_target` can stay or go with it.'
